title: How the JVM makes Java platform-independent
answer: The JVM is the key runtime layer behind Java's platform independence. Java source is compiled into platform-neutral bytecode rather than directly into one operating system's native machine code. A JVM implementation for Windows, Linux, macOS, or another supported platform loads and verifies that bytecode, resolves classes, manages memory, interprets or JIT-compiles frequently executed bytecode into native instructions for that machine, and executes the program. This is the basis of the “write once, run anywhere” model: the same compatible bytecode can run on different systems when an appropriate JVM and required dependencies are available. Platform independence is not absolute when an application depends on native libraries, OS-specific paths, external services, or environment-specific behavior.

steps.title: Start from platform-neutral Java source
steps.question: Java developers write source code without embedding the CPU instruction set of one operating system into each class. When you open AeroTopo's Java entry point, what does that source-level separation suggest about where platform-specific execution responsibility must eventually be handled?
steps.why: Source Java stays at the language level while platform-specific execution is handled later by the runtime layer.
steps.why_te: AeroTopoApplication.java ni open chesi relevant code ni chuddam. Source Java high-level language rules meeda untundi. Windows leda Linux machine instructions direct ga source lo rayamu.

steps.title: Confirm the Java language and SDK baseline
steps.question: Platform independence does not mean a project has no Java-version requirements, because bytecode and APIs still target a chosen Java level. Why should AeroTopo explicitly declare and use Java 21 even though the JVM enables the program to run across operating systems?
steps.why: A Java baseline defines bytecode compatibility and available APIs; platform independence is not the same as version independence.
steps.why_te: Project SDK ikkada kanipistundi. AeroTopo Java 21 use chestunda ani easy ga check cheyyachu. IntelliJ wrong JDK use chesthe compile errors kanipinchachu.

steps.title: Open the build terminal before compilation
steps.question: The terminal exposes compilation and runtime as separate stages rather than hiding them behind one IDE control. The platform-independent execution path becomes clearer when compilation and runtime are viewed as separate stages instead of one IDE button. Why should you use the integrated terminal to observe how AeroTopo moves from Java source toward JVM-executable bytecode?
steps.why: The terminal exposes compilation and runtime as separate stages rather than hiding them behind one IDE control.
steps.why_te: IntelliJ terminal ni open chesi commands run cheddam. Terminal commands compile stage mariyu runtime stage ni separate ga visible chestayi. IDE abstraction venaka jarige process ni direct ga observe cheyyadaniki idi useful.

steps.title: Compile AeroTopo into JVM bytecode
steps.question: The Java compiler does not normally emit Windows x64 or Linux ARM machine instructions directly; it produces class-file bytecode for the JVM specification. How does running the Maven compile phase demonstrate the portable intermediate representation that separates source code from a particular host machine?
steps.why: Maven compile converts Java source into class-file bytecode targeted at the JVM specification.
steps.why_te: Ee command run chesi output ni chudandi. Maven compile Java source ni `.class` bytecode ga transform chestundi. Ee bytecode JVM specification ni target chestundi kabatti same compiled form different supported operating systems lo JVM dwara execute avvachu.

steps.title: Inspect the runtime classpath
steps.question: The JVM must still resolve all required classes and dependencies at runtime. A JVM cannot execute bytecode in isolation when an enterprise application depends on framework and library classes. Why is the runtime classpath part of the platform-independence story even though the bytecode format itself is designed to be portable?
steps.why: The JVM must still resolve all required classes and dependencies at runtime.
steps.why_te: Classpath lo application classes and required libraries ekkada unnayo kanipistayi. Dependency missing ayithe program start avvakapovachu.

data.purpose: Classes and libraries resolved by the JVM

steps.title: Inspect the JVM runtime layer
steps.question: Each operating system needs a JVM implementation that understands the same bytecode specification while translating execution into that machine's native behavior. What responsibilities should you expect the JVM to handle between portable class files and the host operating system?
steps.why: The JVM bridges portable bytecode to host execution through loading, verification, JIT/interpreter work, memory management, and runtime services.
steps.why_te: JVM view lo Java program runtime lo ela execute avutundo chudachu. Class loading, bytecode verification and JIT lanti steps ikkada kanipistayi.

steps.title: Verify the installed runtime implementation
steps.question: The same Java program can move between machines only when each machine has a compatible runtime implementation available. Why does checking `java --version` matter when diagnosing whether a supposedly portable Java application can actually start on a specific environment?
steps.why: Portability depends on a compatible JVM being available on the target environment.
steps.why_te: Ee command run chesi output ni chudandi. Portable application ki compatible JVM implementation installed undali. `java --version` active runtime version/vendor ni confirm chestundi kabatti environment compatibility ni verify cheyyachu.

steps.title: Run the Java application through the JVM
steps.question: Compilation creates bytecode, but platform independence becomes useful only when the host JVM loads and executes that bytecode on the current machine. What does successfully launching AeroTopo through Java demonstrate about the separation between portable program representation and platform-specific runtime execution?
steps.why: A successful launch demonstrates that portable bytecode and the host-specific JVM cooperate to produce execution.
steps.why_te: Run the Java application through the JVM ni simple ga chuddam. Application bytecode same Java model ni follow chestundi. current host JVM danini load chesi native machine meeda execute chestundi.
